correctness.rationale: For different-part red/blue swaps, independent direct evaluation yields the same gain (r_i-r_j-1)/[(m-1)k] to both parties. A profitable swap exists exactly when the maximum and minimum red part occupancies differ by at least two. The exact welfare polynomial is a negative quadratic in the occupancy counts, whose integral optimizers are exactly balanced. Combinatorial enumeration gives all stable colorings. In two-seat parts, every move converts one all-minority and one all-majority pair to mixed pairs, so all paths have initial T steps. A multinomial allocation count and indicator moment identities prove the full distribution, expectation, and variance. The supplied independent exact-rational implementation checks 10,048 placements across 63 equal-part cases and 23,520 profitable swap instances across two-seat cases. It separately tests a nonlinear-part-size counterexample and nonunique clock for 3-seat parts. The proof covers all integers in the stated domain; finite experiments are supplementary.

evidence: Agarwal et al. 2019 regular-graph social price of stability equals one, a strict existential statement.
Bilò et al. 2022 provide global price-of-anarchy bounds and finite-improvement results for regular graphs, but not exact unity for this subfamily nor its clock distribution.
Kreisel et al. 2021 focus on NP-hardness and robustness.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal regular-graph potential theorem guarantees monotone progress and an optimal equilibrium but does not imply that all local extrema are global. No inspected stronger statement forces the occupancy spread at most one, enumerates all equilibria, or gives a fixed number of swaps for every choice of moves on the matching complement. Inefficiency examples for other regular graphs do not contradict the special-family optimum.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Agarwal et al. provide the existential implication (global optimum ⇒ equilibrium), whereas the claim additionally proves (equilibrium ⇒ global optimum) on the specified graph family, using the exact move criterion. Bilò et al. show improvement paths terminate, but this does not imply all paths from one state have equal length, still less the full uniform-start distribution. Kreisel et al. do not supply equivalent structural or probabilistic classification.

evidence: Agarwal et al. (2019) analyze swap-stability and regular-graph welfare, but not the claimed equal-part multipartite occupancy equivalence.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Rewriting the result as discrete balancing of red occupancies, local minimization of a quadratic potential, or segregation on the complement of equal cliques yields an equivalent statement; the public-source search and close full-text examination did not reveal those equivalences as existing theorems. General potential monotonicity alone does not assert absence of suboptimal local maxima.

value.rationale: Identifies a mathematically natural infinite class of densely connected communities in which strict selfish swaps cannot trap the system in a socially suboptimal equilibrium, versus known nontrivial price of anarchy on general regular networks. Gives the complete labeled equilibrium spectrum and a strategy-independent exact convergence-time random variable on the complement-of-matching family, with full distribution, moments and welfare gain. Natural unequal-part and larger-part counterexamples delimit the results. This is a structural finite-population social dynamics classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a routine reparameterization.
